newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Lindsey - concern warranted on stock market.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Lindsey - concern warranted on stock market.

text.p: Outgoing Federal Reserve Governor Lawrence Lindsey on Friday said concern was warranted on the stock market but it was unclear that the situation would pose a problem.

"I think whenever you have something that may look like or turn into a bubble, you have to be concerned, but concern, I think, is the right word," Lindsey said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Lindsey was responding to a question regarding a recent speech in which Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan used the phrase "irrational exuberance" in relation to financial markets.
The comment roiled world markets as traders interpreted it to mean that the Fed chief was worried about the extent of the advance in U.S. stock prices.
But Lindsey said the chairman was simply asking a rhetoricial question: "How can we tell when good news with regards to the stock market turns into irrational exuberance?"
"I don't think we have an answer," Lindsey said.

Turning to the subject of the U.S. economy, Lindsey said that there were risks both to upside and the downside. He cited a possibility that upward pressure on wages could translate into higher prices but said it has not happened yet.

"We are seeing upward pressure on wages. It is certainly conceivable we will see the beginnings of some upward pressure on prices but that doesn't mean we've seen it to date," Lindsey said. "So I think that again we're in a very close monitoring stage."
He said there was "not a lot of room for error" for the Fed with the economy growing at its maximum sustainable pace.
He pointed out that restructuring of the U.S. economy as a result of deregulation has caused it to run more smoothly, easing the inflation threat.
"You don't encounter the bottlenecks that you would normally encounter which also could cause inflation," he said.
Concerning overall inflation, he said, "I think the public views inflation as well under control and I think that perception is warranted and probably will continue for some time."

Lindsey has announced his intention to leave the Fed on Feb. 5 to take up a job at the American Enterprise Institute think tank. He does not plan to participate in the next meeting of the central bank's policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee on Feb 4-5.
